subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers replace the dirty fork PR with a fresh maintainer-controlled fix, or ask the fork author to refresh that branch first?
rationale: The bug is narrow and source-proven, but an open fork PR already references this issue with closing syntax and current labels ask ClawSweeper not to create a new fix PR automatically.

options.title: Replace With Narrow Same-Repo Fix
options.body: Open or adopt a maintainer-controlled PR that covers current sync and async session-list title paths, then close the stale fork PR once a viable replacement exists.

options.title: Ask Fork Author To Refresh
options.body: Keep the fork PR as the candidate only if the author rebases, resolves conflicts, and supplies real TUI or Gateway behavior proof.

options.title: Defer To Broader Title Work
options.body: Leave the bug open until broader session-title work lands, accepting that metadata can still appear in current TUI session titles.

recommendation.title: Replace With Narrow Same-Repo Fix
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a maintainer-controlled PR that covers current sync and async session-list title paths, then close the stale fork PR once a viable replacement exists.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sits at the gateway session-list/TUI title boundary where steipete committed the original path and later performance work.
